Alpine's postgresql16 16.15-r0 is the upgrade to upstream 16.15 and lists CVE-2026-15742 under its secfixes: https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/859fa0795e895af033fab32094a83301f2b4d8ff/community/postgresql16/APKBUILD. The DHI postgresql16 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built from that APKBUILD and the upstream source release of the same version, and the postgres server binary in every published build (16.13-r0, 16.14-r0, 16.15-r0 and 16.16-r0), on both x86_64 and aarch64, reports the matching PostgreSQL 16 release. The fuzzystrmatch module is present: fuzzystrmatch.so ships in the postgresql16-contrib package of every published build for Alpine 3.23, on both x86_64 and aarch64. The earlier published builds for Alpine 3.23 (16.13-r0 and 16.14-r0) are built from earlier upstream releases, their server binaries report those older versions, and Alpine's secfixes do not list this CVE for them, so they are recorded as affected; 16.15-r0 and later carry the fix.

PostgreSQL fixed CVE-2026-15742 (PostgreSQL fuzzystrmatch writes effectively-arbitrary addresses, via integer wraparound) in 17.11 on the PostgreSQL 17 branch: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-15742/ lists 17.11 as the fixed release for major version 17, and the 17.11 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/17.11/, list this CVE. The fix is commit https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/c4d51b62748fd697e5ef4c1108dc77396ba39475 on the REL_17_STABLE branch, 'Avoid overflow in Levenshtein distance calculations.', which changes src/backend/utils/adt/levenshtein.c and src/backend/utils/adt/varlena.c; it is tagged Security: CVE-2026-15742, and it is in the REL_17_11 release tag and not in REL_17_10. The affected code is in the Levenshtein distance code compiled into the PostgreSQL server, /usr/libexec/postgresql17/postgres, in the postgresql17 package, which the fuzzystrmatch extension's levenshtein() and levenshtein_less_equal() call through varstr_levenshtein; fuzzystrmatch.so ships in the postgresql17-contrib package and references varstr_levenshtein in every published build, and the server ships in every published build, on both architectures. The DHI postgresql17 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built from Alpine's postgresql17 APKBUILD, currently https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/ce22298320177ae25085d86fbf3b4fc1150c16a2/main/postgresql17/APKBUILD, which builds the upstream PostgreSQL release tarball; none of the patches it applies, in this or the earlier revisions the published builds came from, touch the source files this fix changes. We checked every published postgresql17 build for Alpine 3.23 (17.7-r0, 17.8-r0, 17.9-r0, 17.10-r0, 17.11-r0 and 17.12-r0) on both x86_64 and aarch64, with package checksums verified against the package index: the server binary of each build reports the PostgreSQL release of the same version (17.7, 17.8, 17.9, 17.10, 17.11 and 17.12). Of these, 17.11-r0 and 17.12-r0 carry the fix, and 17.7-r0, 17.8-r0, 17.9-r0 and 17.10-r0 are affected. The fix adds the error message 'levenshtein distance out of range' to the server; it appears in the server binary of the 17.11-r0 and 17.12-r0 builds and in none of the earlier builds, while the string PostgresMain, our control, is present in every build. fuzzystrmatch.so itself does not carry the fixed code, so the check is made on the server binary. 17.11-r0 is the first published build for Alpine 3.23 that carries the fix. Alpine's postgresql17 APKBUILD lists CVE-2026-15742 under its 17.11-r0 secfixes.

CVE-2026-15742 (PostgreSQL fuzzystrmatch writes effectively-arbitrary addresses, via integer wraparound in levenshtein() and levenshtein_less_equal()) affects PostgreSQL 18 before 18.6 and is fixed upstream in 18.6: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-15742/ and the 18.6 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/18.6/, which also state that 18.5 was never released. Alpine's postgresql18 APKBUILD lists CVE-2026-15742 under its 18.5-r0 secfixes: https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/59a1f1d230675807d5a95a0c1e57ba5d640ba039/main/postgresql18/APKBUILD. This owner has no 18.5-r0 build. In each published build for Alpine 3.23 (18.1-r0, 18.2-r0, 18.3-r0, 18.4-r0, 18.6-r0 and 18.7-r0), on both x86_64 and aarch64, the postgres server binary in the postgresql18 package reports the PostgreSQL release of the same version, and fuzzystrmatch.so ships in the postgresql18-contrib package of the same version, so the affected module is present. 18.6-r0, built from PostgreSQL 18.6, is the first published build for Alpine 3.23 carrying the fix, and 18.6-r0 and 18.7-r0 carry it; the earlier published builds (18.1-r0, 18.2-r0, 18.3-r0 and 18.4-r0) are built from earlier PostgreSQL 18 releases and recorded as affected.

PostgreSQL fixed CVE-2026-15742, integer wraparound in fuzzystrmatch's levenshtein() and levenshtein_less_equal() that lets a user direct writes to a huge range of addresses, in 17.11. Within major version 17, releases before 17.11 are affected. https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-15742/, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/17.11/. Debian fixed it for trixie in postgresql-17 17.11-0+deb13u1 (DSA-6438-1): https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-15742. The fixed version is this owner's first rebuild of Debian's 17.11-0+deb13u1, which packages PostgreSQL 17.11 and is no longer in the repository. Every build published now carries the fix: the postgres server binary reports PostgreSQL 17.11 in the current rebuild of Debian's 17.11-0+deb13u1 and in the 17.11-1 build, and PostgreSQL 17.12 in the 17.12-0 build and in the rebuild of Debian's 17.12-0+deb13u1, on amd64 and arm64. The earlier rebuild of Debian's 17.10-0+deb13u1, no longer in the repository, packages PostgreSQL 17.10; it is affected and sorts below the fixed version.
